name: Bug Reproduce
description: Turn a known bug into a tight, red-capable reproducer (failing test / script), then PROVE the reproducer actually locks that bug with a reversal negative control: reintroduce the bug and the reproducer must go red again. A reproducer that stays green when the bug is put back is a fake and fails the task.

sampleTasks.title: Reproduce a clamp() lower-bound bug and prove the lock with a reversal
sampleTasks.prompt:
Run the bug-reproduce skill on this known bug. BUG: a `clamp(x, lo, hi)` helper ignores its lower bound — it returns `Math.min(x, hi)` so `clamp(-5, 0, 10)` wrongly returns -5 instead of 0. Build a tight, deterministic reproducer in a throwaway dir and PROVE it locks the bug with a reversal negative control. Run these exact steps and report the observed exit codes: (1) `d=.e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce && rm -rf "$d" && mkdir -p "$d"` — a clean, deterministic workspace that is REPO-RELATIVE and SURVIVES the run. Do NOT use `mktemp -d`: the reproducer you build IS the evidence and it is re-read off disk after the run, so a temp dir you delete at the end destroys exactly the artifact the acceptance re-verifies (`.e2e-tmp/` is gitignored, so this pollutes nothing); (2) write `"$d"/clamp.mjs` containing the BUGGY version: `export const clamp = (x, lo, hi) => Math.min(x, hi);`; (3) write the reproducer `"$d"/repro.mjs`: `import assert from 'node:assert'; import { clamp } from './clamp.mjs'; assert.strictEqual(clamp(-5, 0, 10), 0, 'clamp must respect lower bound'); console.log('REPRO OK');`; (4) run the reproducer command `node "$d"/repro.mjs; echo "exit=$?"` — it MUST fail (AssertionError, non-zero exit): this is the bug reproduced RED; (5) apply the minimal fix — rewrite `"$d"/clamp.mjs` to `export const clamp = (x, lo, hi) => Math.max(lo, Math.min(x, hi));` — and re-run `node "$d"/repro.mjs; echo "exit=$?"`: it MUST now pass (exit 0) GREEN; (6) REVERSAL NEGATIVE CONTROL (load-bearing): revert the fix by EDITING `"$d"/clamp.mjs` DIRECTLY back to the buggy one-line body — do NOT use `git stash` / `git checkout` for this: you are in a SHARED working tree with other sessions' uncommitted changes, and stashing would revert THEIR work too. Re-run `node "$d"/repro.mjs; echo "exit=$?"` — it MUST go RED again (non-zero). This proves the reproducer is red-capable ON THIS bug, not accidentally green; (7) restore the fix, confirm GREEN one last time, and LEAVE `.e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce/` in place — do not delete it.

--- YOUR REPORT MUST USE THIS MACHINE-CHECKED OUTPUT CONTRACT (it is re-verified against the filesystem, so a reproducer you never actually wrote is caught):

Line 1 — the reproducer anchor, exactly this shape (the symbol is re-read off disk and must really occur in that file):
`CHANGE-POINT: clamp @ .e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce/clamp.mjs`

Then the RED→GREEN→REVERSAL phase table — one row per phase you actually ran, the FIRST CELL being the `path:line` in your reproducer/subject that the phase turns on (copy the line number from `cat -n` or `rg -n` over the files you just wrote; a missing file, an out-of-range line or a blank line FAILS the report):
```
| path:line | phase | command | exit | observed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| .e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce/repro.mjs:3 | 1 RED (buggy) | node .e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce/repro.mjs | 1 | AssertionError: clamp must respect lower bound |
| .e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce/clamp.mjs:1 | 2 GREEN (fixed) | node .e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce/repro.mjs | 0 | REPRO OK |
| .e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce/repro.mjs:3 | 3 REVERSAL RED | node .e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce/repro.mjs | 1 | AssertionError: clamp must respect lower bound |
```
You need at least 3 phase rows carrying a verified `path:line`, and at least 2 of your citations must land on a line that LITERALLY CONTAINS `clamp` — a real line that is not a real hit in the reproducer is not evidence.

HARD RULE: do not guess line numbers. Every `path:line` anywhere in your report is re-read off disk AFTER the run, so the files must still be there. Citations MUST be repo-root-relative (`.e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce/repro.mjs:3`, never an absolute path and never a `/tmp/...` path, which cannot be resolved from the repo root).

Report: the exact reproducer command you ran, the initial RED (exit code + the assertion that failed), the GREEN after the fix (exit 0), and the reversal RED after reintroducing the bug (exit code) — that reversal is the whole point: it is how you know the reproducer locks the bug.
expectedArtifacts: the reproducer left on disk at `.e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce/` (repo-relative, survives the run) + a `CHANGE-POINT: clamp @ .e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce/clamp.mjs` declaration
RED→GREEN→REVERSAL phase table: ≥3 rows whose first cell is a `path:line` that resolves on disk, ≥2 landing on a line containing `clamp`
the exact reproducer command (a `node repro.mjs` invocation) that was actually run
initial RED: the reproducer failed on the buggy code (AssertionError, non-zero exit)
reversal negative control: reintroducing the bug makes the reproducer RED again (non-zero exit) — proves the lock

acceptanceCriteria.label: the reproducer REALLY EXISTS on disk — anchored on `clamp @ .e2e-tmp/apc/bug-reproduce/clamp.mjs`, every path:line re-read off disk, ≥2 citations landing on a line that actually contains the subject symbol, ≥3 phase rows (RED/GREEN/REVERSAL) carrying a verified citation
names a concrete runnable reproducer command (node/test invocation)
initial RED: reproducer fails on the bug (assertion / non-zero exit)
REVERSAL negative control: reintroducing the bug makes the reproducer RED again (the lock)
acceptanceCriteria.match: ((revert|reversal|revers\w*|reintroduc|re-?inject|re-?insert|put(ting)?\s+(the\s+)?bug\s+back|remov\w*\s+the\s+fix|back\s?out|stash|undo\s+the\s+fix|buggy\s*(version|body|one-?liner|代码|码|恢复|复原)|反转|复原|放回|重新(注入|引入)|注入回|撤(掉|回|销)\s*(了\s*)?(修复|fix))[\s\S]{0,220}(fail\w*|red\b|❌|✗|assert\w*|non-?zero|exit(\s*code)?[^0-9]{0,6}[1-9]))|((fail\w*|red\b|❌|✗|assert\w*|non-?zero|exit(\s*code)?[^0-9]{0,6}[1-9])[\s\S]{0,220}(revert|reversal|revers\w*|reintroduc|re-?inject|re-?insert|put(ting)?\s+(the\s+)?bug\s+back|remov\w*\s+the\s+fix|back\s?out|stash|undo\s+the\s+fix|buggy\s*(version|body|one-?liner|代码|码|恢复|复原)|反转|复原|放回|重新(注入|引入)|注入回|撤(掉|回|销)\s*(了\s*)?(修复|fix)))
